entries.input: Let $\sum c_n z^n$ be a complex power series and suppose $|c_n|^{1/n} \to \alpha$. The series converges when $|z| \alpha < 1$ and diverges when $|z| \alpha > 1$.
entries.name: PowerSeriesRadiusOfConvergence
entries.binders: (c : ℕ → ℂ) (α : ℝ) (hα : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ‖c n‖ ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) Filter.atTop (nhds α)) (z : ℂ)
entries.conclusion: (‖z‖ * α < 1 → Summable (fun n => c n * z ^ n)) ∧ (1 < ‖z‖ * α → ¬ Summable (fun n => c n * z ^ n))
entries.witness_note: Satisfiable: `c = 0`, `α = 0`, `z = 0`; see the root-test entry for why the limit is not a one-line term.

entries.input: The power series $\sum n^3 z^n$ converges exactly for $|z| < 1$.
entries.name: RadiusOfNCubedSeries
entries.conclusion: Summable (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℂ) ^ 3 * z ^ n) ↔ ‖z‖ < 1

entries.input: The power series $\sum 2^n z^n / n!$ converges for every complex $z$.
entries.name: RadiusOfTwoPowOverFactorialSeries
entries.conclusion: Summable (fun n : ℕ => 2 ^ n / (n.factorial : ℂ) * z ^ n)

entries.input: The power series $\sum 2^n z^n / n^2$ converges exactly for $|z| \leq 1/2$.
entries.name: RadiusOfTwoPowOverNSquaredSeries
entries.conclusion: Summable (fun n : ℕ => 2 ^ n / ((n : ℂ) ^ 2) * z ^ n) ↔ ‖z‖ ≤ 1 / 2

entries.input: If a power series $\sum c_n z^n$ has integer coefficients, infinitely many of which are nonzero, then it diverges for every $z$ with $|z| > 1$.
entries.name: IntegerCoefficientPowerSeriesRadiusAtMostOne
entries.binders: (c : ℕ → ℤ) (h : Set.Infinite {n | c n ≠ 0}) (z : ℂ) (hz : 1 < ‖z‖)
entries.conclusion: ¬ Summable (fun n => (c n : ℂ) * z ^ n)
entries.witness: ⟨fun _ => 1, by simpa using (Set.infinite_univ : (Set.univ : Set ℕ).Infinite), 2, by simp, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4$ be complex numbers of modulus $1$, none of them equal to $1$. Prove that $3 - z_1 - z_2 - z_3 - z_4 + z_1 z_2 z_3 z_4 \neq 0$.
entries.name: Putnam2020B5
entries.binders: (z₁ z₂ z₃ z₄ : ℂ) (h₁ : ‖z₁‖ = 1) (h₂ : ‖z₂‖ = 1) (h₃ : ‖z₃‖ = 1) (h₄ : ‖z₄‖ = 1) (n₁ : z₁ ≠ 1) (n₂ : z₂ ≠ 1) (n₃ : z₃ ≠ 1) (n₄ : z₄ ≠ 1)
entries.conclusion: 3 - z₁ - z₂ - z₃ - z₄ + z₁ * z₂ * z₃ * z₄ ≠ 0
entries.title: Putnam 2020 B5
entries.witness: ⟨-1, -1, -1, -1, by simp, by simp, by simp, by simp, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4$ be complex numbers of modulus $1$. Prove that $3 - z_1 - z_2 - z_3 - z_4 + z_1 z_2 z_3 z_4 \neq 0$.
entries.name: Putnam2020B5Twin
entries.conclusion: 3 - z₁ - z₂ - z₃ - z₄ + z₁ * z₂ * z₃ * z₄ ≠ 0
entries.title: Putnam 2020 B5, the hypothesis $z_j \neq 1$ dropped
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2020-b5`, and the archetypal one: the four hypotheses $z_j \neq 1$ are removed and nothing else changes. Taking every $z_j = 1$ gives $3 - 4 + 1 = 0$, so the conclusion fails on the single point the dropped hypothesis excluded. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.
entries.witness: ⟨-1, -1, -1, -1, by simp, by simp, by simp, by simp, trivial⟩
